column6: Self-adjoint skew quartics, symplectic monodromy, and zeta functions
column7: For an odd prime power $P$, let $A_H(P)$ be the number of $a\in\F_{P^H}$ for which the self-adjoint skew quartic $t^4+t^3+at^2+t+1$ is irreducible in $\F_{P^H}[t;σ]$, with $σ(c)=c^P$. We determine $A_H(3)$ for every $H\ge1$ and prove that its minimal constant-coefficient recurrence has order $24$. Local ramification gives the degrees of the Steinberg and regular cuspidal Frobenius polynomials. Duality and finitely many exact counts determine both polynomials. For $P=p^f$ with $p\nmid f$, we construct an explicit genus-$P(P+1)/2$ flag curve whose zeta numerator is the Steinberg Frobenius polynomial. At $P=3$ this identifies the degree-$12$ factor computed above with the zeta numerator of a genus-$6$ curve. For general $P$ the flag curve and the regular cuspidal factors give a rational expression for the counting series. We evaluate the linear coefficients of the two factors by an elliptic-curve point count and express their quadratic coefficients through a single finite-field character sum.

column6: On Jacquet Modules of Principal Series in Families
column7: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over a $p$-adic field $F$. Let $Y$ be the diagonalizable affine group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}[p^{-1},p^{1/2}]$ parametrizing weakly unramified characters of a minimal Levi $M$. The relative Weyl group $W$ acts on $Y$. We define a coherent sheaf $\mathcal{J}$, called the universal Jacquet module, on the fiber product $Y\times_{Y/\!/W}Y$. The fibers of $\mathcal{J}$ can be identified with the duals of spaces of intertwining operators between weakly unramified principal series representations of $G$. We use the geometry of $Y\times_{Y/\!/W}Y$ to study the fundamental properties of $\mathcal{J}$. In particular, we determine the invertible locus of $\mathcal{J}$. Thus we show that for any field $k$ with $\operatorname{char}k\neq p, p^{1/2}\in k$ and any weakly unramified character $χ\in Y(k)$, the normalized Jacquet module $π_{χ,N}$ of the normalized parabolic induction $π_χ=\operatorname{ind}_P^Gχ$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}(χ\times_{Y/\!/W}Y)$ as an $\mathcal{O}(Y)$-module if and only if $\operatorname{End}_G(π_χ)\cong k$. This addresses the precise non-semisimple structure of Jacquet modules in the scalar endomorphism case. Specializing to the case in which $G$ is split, $χ$ is trivial, and $k=\mathbb{C}$, this proves a conjecture of Dipendra Prasad. We also show that the isomorphism $π_{χ,N}\cong\mathcal{O}(χ\times_{Y/\!/W}Y)$ cannot be defined canonically over the family of characters $χ$ satisfying $\operatorname{End}_G(π_χ)\cong\mathbb{C}$, by showing that the restriction of $\mathcal{J}$ to its invertible locus is a nontrivial line bundle if the relative root system of $G$ contains an irreducible component of rank at least two.

column5: Yiqun Chen; Rupert L. Frank; Jie Xiao; Dachun Yang; Wen Yuan; Yangyang Zhang
column6: Sharp Fractional Capacitary-Distance Hardy Inequalities
column7: Let $d\in\mathbb N$, $p\in(1,\infty)$, $p':=\frac{p}{p-1}$, and $s\in(0,\min\{1+\frac1p,\frac dp\})$. For an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, let $F:=\mathbb{R}^d\setminusΩ$. For any $α\in(0,1]$ and $x\inΩ$, let \begin{align*} d_{α,s,p}(x) :=\inf\left\{r\in(0,\infty): \frac{\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{F\cap B(x,r)})} {\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{B(x,r)})}\geα\right\}, \end{align*} where $\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}$ is the capacity associated with the fractional Sobolev energy $[\,\cdot\,]_{s,p}^p$. In this article, we prove that there exists a positive constant $C$, depending only on $d$, $s$, and $p$, such that, for any $α\in(0,1]$ and $u\in C_{\rm c}^\infty(Ω)$, \begin{align*} \int_Ω\frac{|u(x)|^p}{d_{α,s,p}(x)^{sp}}\,dx \le Cα^{-p'}[u]_{s,p}^p. \end{align*} We also show that both the exponent $p'$ in $α^{-p'}$ as $α\to0^+$ over the class of all open sets and the range $s\in(0,1+\frac1p)$ within $sp<d$ are sharp. Our proofs use variational minimization, equilibrium measures on trees, and weighted Hardy inequalities.

column5: Fan Bu; Dachun Yang; Wen Yuan
column6: Sharp Weak-Type Inequalities for Scalar and Matrix Weights
column7: Let $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $p':=\frac p{p-1}$. In this article, we establish a mixed multiplier weak-type inequality with weight dependence $[w]_{A_p}^{\frac1p}[w]_{A_\infty}^{\max\{\frac1p,\frac1{p'}\}}$ for scalar $A_p$ weights and Calderón--Zygmund operators whose modulus of continuity satisfies the Dini condition. As a consequence, we obtain the sharp exponent $\max\{1,\frac2p\}$ of $[w]_{A_p}$ in the corresponding pure $A_p$ bound. Moreover, in the matrix-weighted setting, we prove the sharpness of the exponent $1+\min\{\frac1p,\frac1{p(p-1)}\}$ of $[W]_{\mathcal A_p}$ in the known multiplier weak-type inequality for the Hilbert transform.

column5: Zhengyun Nie; Anant Shyam; Brian Bullins
column6: Bias-Reduced and Parallel Heavy-Tailed Stochastic Convex Optimization in $\ell_p$ Geometries
column7: We consider the fundamental problem of parallel stochastic convex optimization (SCO), whose aim is to approximately minimize a convex objective when given the ability to query a moment-bounded stochastic gradient oracle multiple times in parallel per round. Whereas most previous results have focused on the variance-bounded Euclidean ($\ell_2$-norm) setting, meaning the objective is Lipschitz with respect to the $\ell_2$-norm over an $\ell_2$-bounded feasible set in $\mathbb{R}^d$, in this work we study parallel SCO in $\ell_p$ settings for $2 \le p < \infty$ under a heavy-tailed noise model. We begin by introducing a new class of $\ell_p$-optimal-distance-convergence (ODC$_p$) algorithms, drawing on prior stochastic bias-reduced techniques [ACJ+21], which combine with multilevel Monte Carlo methods to efficiently estimate the optimum of uniformly convex objectives. As a consequence of our ODC$_p$ algorithms, we first establish rates for projection-efficient $\ell_p$-Lipschitz optimization, composite convex minimization, and efficient $\ell_p$-proximal point estimation. Combining our ODC$_p$ algorithms with a new $\ell_p$-generalized Gaussian-based stochastic gradient estimator ($p$-GREG), we provide two efficient $\ell_p$ parallel algorithms, EpochDA and $\ell_p$-AC-SA, which achieve optimization error $ε> 0$ with at most $\tilde{O}(d^{\frac{p}{2p + 2}} ε^{-\frac{p}{p + 1}})$ query depth, improving upon the sequential heavy-tailed stochastic query depth of $O(ε^{-p})$ for $ε\leq \tilde{O}(d^{-1/(2p)})$. We also establish dimension-dependent lower bounds of $Ω\bigl(\min\{ε^{-p},d^{p/(3p-2)}\}\bigr)$ adaptive rounds for nonsmooth convex optimization over a subset of the unit $\ell_p$ ball. Our results improve upon the $Ω(\min\{ε^{-p},ε^{2/3}d^{1/3}\})$ bounds of [DG19], when adapted to the same feasible set.

column5: Feng Liu; Yongzhi Lian; Yanzhen Wang
column6: Sharp L^p and variation inequalities for maximal operators on finite connected graphs
column7: Let $G=(V_G,E_G)$ be a finite connected graph (here $V_G$ and $E_G$ denote the set of vertices and edges of $G$ respectively). The primary aim of this paper is to study the sharp variation and $L^p$ inequalities of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator $M_G$ defined on $G$ and its fractional variant $M_{α,G}\,(0<α<1)$). Set $${\bf C}_{α,G}^{p,q}=\sup\limits_{{\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)>0}\frac{{\rm Var}_{q,G}(M_{α,G}f)}{{\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)},$$ where ${\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)$ denotes the $p$-variation of $f$ on $G$. We denote by $K_n$ (resp., $S^n$) the complete (resp., star) graph with $n\geq4$ vertices. When $α=0$, we prove ${\bf C}_{α,S_n}^{p,p} =1-\frac{1}{n}$ for $0<p<1$. This solve a question originally posed by Liu and Xue in 2021. In the fractional case $0<α<1$, we prove ${\bf C}_{α,S_n}^{1,q}=1-n^{-α}$ and ${\bf C}_{α,K_n}^{1,q} =(1-n^{α-1})(n-1)^{-α}$ for $q=\frac{1}{1-α}$, which provide some examples focusing on sharp variation inequalities of fractional maximal operators. The sharp variation inequalities of uncentered fractional maximal operators are also established. In addition, the sharp $L^p$ inequalities of uncentered fractional maximal operator $\widetilde{M}_{α,G}$ are also studied. More precisely, we obtain lower bounds and upper bounds for $C_{q,G}$ such that the inequality $\|\widetilde{M}_{α,G}f\|_q\leq C_{q,G}\|f\|_p$ holds and the complete graphs $K_n$ and star graphs $S_n$ are two extreme graphs that reach the lower bound and upper bound respectively.

column6: The closure of the nonreal roots of bounded-height polynomials is connected exactly at pronic heights
column7: Let C_h be the closure of the nonreal roots of integer polynomials with coefficients of modulus at most h. With the nonzero real roots included, the closure is connected at every height; without them, connectedness becomes arithmetic. We prove that C_h is connected exactly when h=q(q-1) is a pronic number 2, 6, 12, 20, ..., and has at least five components otherwise. At height two this confirms a twenty-year-old numerical observation of Shmerkin and Solomyak on double zeros of power series: apart from 1/2 they form the interval $[1/ρ,1)=C_2\cap(0,1)$, with $ρ$ the tribonacci constant. Disconnection is almost always infinite. For (p-1)^2<h<=p^2-3, $h\neq p(p-1)$, infinitely many components with nonempty interior accumulate at $\pm p$ and $\pm 1/p$, and when h<p(p-1) these four points are themselves components. Next to each square q^2>=16, at least two of the three heights q^2-2, q^2-1, q^2 have infinitely many components accumulating at a common point of (1/(q+1),1/q). Explicit series give infinitely many components at every nonpronic height below 167 other than 1, 3, 4, 9, 25, 63 and 81, and in general at most sqrt(X)+1 nonpronic heights h<=X can have finitely many components, although C_h is a Peano compactum at every height. The proofs compare values and derivatives of all admissible power series near a real double zero; the comparison sets are open and closed in the whole core, so components separated near the axis cannot reconnect elsewhere. On the real axis, the double zeros at heights 1, 3, 4, 7 form sets with infinitely many components; at height one this proves a conjecture of Shmerkin and Solomyak and one of Solomyak on the connectedness locus for pairs of affine maps.

column5: Jian Chen; Shaojie Yang; Zhaoyang Yin
column6: Local well-posedness, wave breaking and ill-posedness for the unidirectional non-local wave model
column7: In this paper, we first establish local well-posedness (existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence) for the Cauchy problem associated with the unidirectional non-local wave model in the Besov spaces $B^s_{p,r}$ with $s>1+\frac{1}{p}$ and $1\leq p,r\leq\infty$, as well as in the critical Besov spaces $B^{1+\frac{1}{p}}_{p,1}$ with $1\leq p<\infty$. Next, by exploiting the fine structure of the equation and performing a delicate analysis of the commutator terms, we establish a new sufficient condition for wave breaking without using any conservation law. Finally, we prove that the model is ill-posed in $B^{1+\frac{1}{p}}_{p,r}$ for $1\leq p\leq\infty$ and $1<r\leq\infty$. Our analysis further clarifies the well-posedness theory and wave-breaking behavior of the unidirectional non-local wave model arising from the motion of a cold plasma in a magnetic field, which refines and improves previously known related results.

column5: Yujiao Jiang; Yuk-Kam Lau; Guangshi Lü
column6: An asymptotic formula for primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$
column7: We prove Motohashi's conjecture on primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$, with Iwaniec's corrected constant. Let $b$ denote the characteristic function of the positive integers representable as a sum of two squares. Then, as $x\to\infty$, \[ \sum_{p\le x}b(p-1) =κ\Spr\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}} +O\!\left(\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}\sqrt{\log\log x}}\right), \] where $κ$ is the Landau--Ramanujan constant and $\Spr=\prod_{p\equiv3\,({\rm mod}\,4)}\bigl(1-1/(p(p-1))\bigr)$. The proof combines auxiliary prime factors with a mean square estimate for bilinear sums. We obtain the minor arc bound through harmonic switching and high moments, replacing arithmetic divisibility conditions by independent projective lines. We remove the auxiliary weights using Selberg's sieve.

column6: Total Variation Regularized Barycenters in Wasserstein Space
column7: We study total variation regularization of Wasserstein barycenters on bounded connected Lipschitz domains. We prove existence for arbitrary prescribed probability measures and uniqueness when at least one is absolutely continuous. Our main results are attained dual formulations in terms of relative perimeters and vector fields with zero normal trace. These yield necessary and sufficient optimality conditions and a variational characterization of superlevel sets. We also establish a maximum principle on convex domains, stability of minimizers, and an exact reduction to a single TV-JKO step in one dimension. The existence, uniqueness, and perimeter duality results extend to costs $|x-y|^p$, $p>1$, under the same assumptions.

column6: Second-order geometric consistency of nonlinear FE-HMM on surfaces via corrector non-degeneracy
column7: We analyze the geometric variational crime of nonlinear finite element heterogeneous multiscale methods (FE--HMM) for $p$-growth monotone laws on curved surfaces, $p\ge2$. The practical method projects discrete gradients onto the exact tangent planes; we compare it with the exactly lifted method on the same discrete space. Without further hypotheses, the difference is $O(h_g^{p/(p-1)})$ in the metric induced by the cell correctors. The optimal order $O(h_g^2)$ holds with a constant given by a weighted negative moment of the corrected gradients, evaluated along the practical solution only; no bounds on discrete gradients in $L^\infty$ are used. The negative moment is a sufficient condition for the lower shifted $p$-structure of the discrete homogenized flux, which for $p>2$ is not available in general. For the model law and a fixed cell mesh, its uniform boundedness is equivalent to a finite-dimensional directional criterion on degenerate correctors, and for laminates it holds with an explicit bound, uniform in the cell mesh. With macro--micro quasi-optimality and an estimate for coefficient sampling, the reconstructed microscopic field converges as $O(h+H^{\min{s,1}}+h_g^2)$, where $H^s$ is the cell approximation rate. Experiments on a torus with an exact closest-point lift and a transported anisotropic $p=4$ material show second-order geometric convergence up to $98,304$ macroscopic quadrature points, each with a fully solved nonlinear cell problem, with bounded a posteriori constants for both load treatments.

column6: Large orbits of $p$-groups on conjugacy classes
column7: Let $P$ be a $p$-group that acts faithfully and coprimely on a finite group $H$. A classical result of D.\ S.\ Passman, in the form proved by I.\ M.\ Isaacs, asserts that there exists an element $x\in H$ such that $|C_P(x)|\le (|P|/p)^{1/p}$. In this paper, we study the corresponding question for the action of $P$ on the conjugacy classes of $H$. We show that for every odd prime $p$ the analogue of Isaacs' bound fails for classes. On the other hand, we prove that if $H$ is solvable, then there always exists a conjugacy class $c$ of $H$ whose stabilizer in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$, and that this bound is best possible for every prime $p$. As a consequence, there always exists an irreducible character of $H$ whose inertia group in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$. The proof proceeds via a result on linear actions of $p$-nilpotent groups, and in the quasiprimitive case it relies on a classification of Holt and Yang and on computer calculations.

column6: A lattice construction of the Kormos-Runkel-Watts defect flows in minimal models
column7: Kormos, Runkel, and Watts (KRW) showed that a topological defect of a diagonal minimal model $M(p,p+1)$, perturbed by a weakly relevant defect field, flows to a new conformal interface. We study the flow of the $(2,1)$ Verlinde defect $D_{(2,1)}$ driven by the spinful defect field $φ_{(1,3)}\otimes\barφ_{(3,3)}$ on the lattice. The flow preserves the $(r,1)$ Verlinde lines. This preserved symmetry makes a dilute RSOS realisation possible. We study this flow numerically using both exact diagonalization and density matrix renormalization group (DMRG). At $p=4$, the flow ends on the invertible line $η=D_{(3,1)}$. At $p=5$ it ends on a non-trivial conformal interface $C_5$ with $g=1.503(2)$ and transmission coefficient $T=0.665(10)$. We report its spectrum, leading irrelevant dimension, and lattice $β$-function. Gauging $η$ maps $C_5$ to an interface of the three-state Potts model, which breaks $\mathbb{Z}_3$ but is a stable interface once the Fibonacci line $τ_{\mathrm{Fib}}$ and charge conjugation are imposed. A loop-model formulation allows us to follow the family $C_p$ at continuous $4\le p\le5$: it moves smoothly from $C_5$ to $η$ as we lower $p$.

column6: A counterexample concerning weighted convolution on the integers
column7: Let $1<p<\infty$ and let $w:\mathbb{Z}\to(0,\infty)$ be a weight. When is the weighted space $\ell^p(\mathbb{Z},w)$ an algebra with respect to convolution? A well-known sufficient condition is that $(w^{-q}*w^{-q})/w^{-q}$ be bounded on $\mathbb{Z}$, where $q:=p/(p-1)$ is the index conjugate to $p$. We present an example to show that this sufficient condition is not necessary.

column6: Dimensional dependence of critical phenomena in black hole interiors
column7: Black hole interiors exhibit a critical transition in which a perturbed inner horizon either survives or collapses into a spacelike singularity, but whether the exponent governing this transition depends on spacetime dimension has remained an open question. In this paper, we numerically investigate the interior dynamics of $D$ dimensional Reissner-Nordström (RN) black holes perturbed by a real scalar field. Strong perturbations destroy the null inner horizon and produce a spacelike singularity, whereas weaker perturbations preserve it with an areal radius that decreases as the perturbation amplitude increases. As the initial scalar field amplitude $p$ approaches its critical value $p^{*}$, the inner horizon radius decreases continuously to zero. Near criticality, this radius obeys the power law $r_{s}\propto|p-p^{*}|^γ$. In four dimensions, different initial scalar field profiles and initial RN black hole charges yield nearly identical critical exponents, $γ\simeq1/2$, supporting the universality of the scaling law. Within the investigated range $4\leq D\leq9$, the critical exponent decreases systematically with increasing spacetime dimension. The numerical results suggest the scaling relation $r_s\propto|p-p^{*}|^{1/(D-2)}$. This result establishes a new dimension-dependent universality class for interior black hole critical phenomena, distinct from the standard Choptuik collapse scaling.

column6: $W^{1,p}$ error estimates of an IPDG and a class of HDG methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains
column7: This paper analyzes a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin (IPDG) method, a hybrid mixed DG method, and two representative hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains. For any fixed $ε\in (0,\frac{1}{2})$, we first derive optimal discrete $W^{1,p}$ error estimates for $2\leq p<\frac{1}ε$ by combining the interface Green's functions developed in \cite{lq2026} with the Fubini-type weighted estimates established in this paper. These error estimates lead to discrete $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup stability for $2\leq q<\frac{1}ε$, where $q$ is the conjugate number of $p$ such that $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$. Using this stability result and a suitably constructed dual problem, we extend the optimal error estimates to $\frac{1}{1-ε}<p<2$ and subsequently establish the corresponding inf-sup stability for $\frac{1}{1-ε}< q<2$. Thus, both optimal discrete $W^{1,p}$ error estimates and discrete $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup stability hold throughout the range $\frac{1}{1-ε}<p<\frac{1}ε$, with $q=p/(p-1)$. Note that all of the aforementioned results are free of logarithmic factors and also hold on polyhedral meshes (except for the hybrid mixed DG method). Compared with the conforming finite element method (FEM), establishing such error estimates and inf-sup stability results for DG methods on convex polyhedral domains is more delicate because their analysis involves mesh-dependent norms. Consequently, the operator interpolation theory employed for conforming FEMs cannot be directly applied to DG methods. Finally, a numerical example is presented to illustrate the theoretical results.

column6: Hölder Duality and Self-Dual Arc Length on $L^p$ Unit Curves
column7: We study arc length on the first-quadrant unit curve $x^p+y^p=1$, $p>1$, when length is measured with respect to an $L^r$ norm. Denoting this length by $L(p,r)$, we prove the Hölder-duality identity $L(p,r)=L(r^*,p^*)$, where $p^*=p/(p-1)$ and $r^*=r/(r-1)$. The identity is interpreted as a special case of the symmetry of mixed area (equivalently, of the anisotropic perimeter pairing). For the distinguished dual metric $r=p^*$, the length element agrees with the areal angular element: $L(p,p^*)=\int_γ(x\,dy-y\,dx)=\frac1p B(1/p,1/p)$. Thus the familiar coincidence between arc length and angular parameter on the Euclidean unit circle is the self-dual case $p=2$ of a more general relation between $L^p$ geometry and its dual metric. As a consequence, the Euclidean arc length of the $L^p$ unit curve admits a dual trigonometric representation.

column5: Yongheng Qin; Yuhua Sun; Jie Xiao
column6: Sharp volume tests and entropy thresholds for quasilinear elliptic inequalities with gradient reactions
column7: We investigate positive weak solutions of $-Δ_m u\ge u^p|\nabla u|^q$ on complete noncompact Riemannian manifolds without curvature, volume doubling, or Poincaré assumptions. For the superhomogeneous mixed reaction we derive a curvature-free integral volume test by combining two first-order estimates with a recurrence for the mass of a \emph{fixed} density. The same approach organizes the pure-gradient and capacity criteria and yields sharp finite hierarchies of iterated-logarithmic growth bounds, with counterexamples on smooth model manifolds. In the subhomogeneous region, vanishing lower growth of $\log V(R)/R^{m-q}$ forces the Liouville property. On the homogeneous line $p+q=m-1$, we obtain the optimal strict lower-volume-entropy threshold $(p+1)((m-1)/p)^{p/(p+1)}$ for $p>0$ (and $1$ for $p=0$), together with examples at equality. The existing six-region classification is not claimed as new; the advances concern refined volume hypotheses and their model sharpness. The tests remain valid for smooth weighted measures and for locally bounded positive Sobolev solutions. Sharpness is understood within the stated model families; no characterization from volume alone on an individual manifold is asserted.

column5: Meng Geng; Dachun Yang; Wen Yuan; Yirui Zhao
column6: Sharp Quantitative Weighted Estimates for Lifted Maximal Operators with Applications
column7: In this article, we establish sharp quantitative weighted estimates for the lifted Hardy--Littlewood (resp Sobolev sharp) maximal operators $\{\mathcal M_θ\}_{θ\in(0,\infty)}$ (resp $\{\mathcal M_θ^\sharp\}_{θ\in(0,\infty)}$). Specifically, for $p\in(1,\infty)$, $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, $\upsilon\in A_p$, and $f\in L^p_\upsilon$, we prove that \begin{align*} \sup_{θ,λ\in(0,\infty)}λ^p \underset{\mathcal M_θ(f)(x,t)>λt^γ} {\int_{\mathbb R^n}\int_0^\infty} t^{γp-1}\,dt\,\upsilon(x)\,dx \lesssim [\upsilon]_{A_p}^{α_{p,γ}} \|f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p, \end{align*} where $α_{p,γ}:=\frac{p}{p-1}$ for $γ\in[-n,0)$ and $α_{p,γ}:=1$ otherwise and where the implicit positive constant depends only on $n$, $p$, and $γ$. For $\mathcal M_θ^\sharp$, the corresponding estimate holds with $\|f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p$ replaced by $\|\nabla f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p$ for any $f\in\dot W^{1,p}_\upsilon$, and with $α_{p,γ}:=\frac{p}{p-1}$ for $γ\in[-1,0)$ and $α_{p,γ}:=1$ otherwise. We show that, for an $A_1$ weight $\upsilon$, the weight constant in the above estimates becomes $[\upsilon]_{A_1}$ for the sharp ranges $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, or $p=1$ and $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus[-n,0]$ (resp. $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus[-1,0]$). We also prove that $α_{p,γ}$ is sharp, and we establish exact limiting formulae and characterize Muckenhoupt weights via weak-type bounds. As applications, we characterize the weighted Hardy(--Sobolev) space $H^1_\upsilon$ with $\upsilon\in A_1$ in terms of the truncated Riesz transforms with optimal range $γ\in \mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$. More applications include the sharp weighted Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and the generalization to ball Banach function spaces.

column5: Yuxuan Zhou; Yingfang Zhang; Wenming Zou
column6: Extremals for Sharp Trace Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev Inequalities on Convex Cones
column7: Zugmeyer~\cite{Zug} established sharp trace Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev inequalities on convex cones for $a\geq n>p>1$. We classify all nonzero real-valued extremals of these inequalities. Let the cone be the epigraph of a finite convex function that is positively homogeneous of degree one, and let $H$ be any norm. We prove that equality holds precisely for functions of the form $A H(x+te+\ell)^{-(a-p)/(p-1)}$, where $A\in\mathbb{R}\backslash\{0\}$, $t>0$, $e=(0,\ldots,0,1)$, and $\ell$ belongs to the largest vector subspace contained in the cone. The result includes the critical Sobolev trace inequality at $a=n$, as well as nonsmooth norms and cones, half-spaces, and cones containing lines.

column5: Akash Deep; Bhathiya Divelgama; A. Alexandre Trindade; W. Brent Lindquist; Svetlozar T. Rachev; Frank J. Fabozzi
column6: Probability-Weighting Functions for Normal Tempered-Stable Laws: Orthogonal Channels and Information-Theoretic Indices
column7: A probability-weighting function (PWF) maps objective probabilities into decision weights. We construct PWFs from changes in the distribution of returns rather than from a parametric family: with prior and posterior return distributions $F_{prior}$ and $F_{post}$, the PWF is $w(p) = F_{post}(F_{prior}^{-1}(p))$. Both distributions are normal tempered-stable (NTS), and the posterior differs from the prior along one of three channels, each isolated with the variance held fixed: scale, skewness and tail thickness. Around a symmetric benchmark with excess kurtosis 3, a 40% change in scale moves cumulative probabilities by up to 7 to 8 percentage points, a skewness of $\pm 0.5$ by 2 percentage points, and a change of $\pm 0.3$ in the tail index by about 2 percentage points. The three channels leave distinct signatures: the deviation $w(p) - p$ changes sign once, twice and three times, respectively. Three information-theoretic indices (a Fisher-normalized logit shift, a signed Jensen-Shannon divergence and a log-odds elasticity) summarize the distortions and avoid the endpoint singularity of the classical ratio $(w(p)-p)/[p(1-p)]$. Applied to NTS parameters calibrated to S&P 500 ETF daily returns over 2015-2025, the same channels produce distortions of 2 to 7 percentage points. Code that reproduces every figure and number in the paper is provided.

column6: A dual variational principle for the Moser-Trudinger inequality: existence, uniqueness and stability of extremals
column7: For $p>1$, with $p'=p/(p-1)$, we prove the sharp dual inequality $$ \int_0^1-\log\left(1-\frac{\left|\int_0^xf(y) dy\right|^{p'}}{x}\right) dx\leq\mathsf{K}_p, \qquad \|f\|_{L^p(0,1)}\leq1, $$ where $\mathsf{K}_p$ is the logarithm of the optimal value in Moser's one-dimensional formulation of the Moser-Trudinger inequality. The dual functional follows from the Gibbs variational principle, monotone transport and the Legendre transform. Its supremum is attained, giving a dual proof of the existence theorems of Carleson-Chang (1986) and Hudson-Leckband (2002); the classical concentration threshold is realized by equality cases in Hoelder's inequality. For $p=2$ we prove, with rigorous computer-assisted estimates, that the nonnegative dual maximizer is unique and nondegenerate. Hence the extremal of the Moser-Trudinger inequality on a disk $D$ is unique up to sign, confirming conjectures of Adimurthi-Karthik-Giacomoni (2016) and of Chen-Lu-Xue-Zhu (2026). The positive extremal $u_*$ is nondegenerate, and, writing $\mathcal{M}_D(u)=|D|^{-1}\int_De^{4πu^2} dx$, we obtain $$ \mathcal{M}_D(u_*)-\mathcal{M}_D(u) \geq c \min_{\pm}\|\nabla(u\mp u_*)\|_{L^2(D)}^2 $$ for all $u\in H_0^1(D)$ with $\|\nabla u\|_{L^2(D)}\leq1$. Here $c>0$, and the exponent two is optimal, giving a quantitative stability theorem of Bianchi-Egnell type.

column5: Moritz Egert; Jan Giesselmann; Marc Hoffmann
column6: Quantitative maximal $\mathrm{L}^p$-regularity for generators of real contraction semigroups
column7: Let $-A$ be the generator of a real, symmetric contraction semigroup on a $σ$-finite measure space. We prove a universal bound for maximal $\mathrm{L}^p$-regularity: In space-time norms $$\|Au\|_p \leq \big(p^* + \tfrac{p^*}{2(p^*-1)}\big) \|f\|_p,$$ where $p^* = \max(p,p/(p-1))$ and $u$ is the mild solution to the Cauchy problem with right-hand side $f$ starting at $u(0)=0$. Linear growth of the constant in $p^*$ is optimal. Our proof introduces an elementary approach to maximal regularity that avoids both vector-valued harmonic analysis and dilation theory. We also obtain quantitative maximal regularity estimates for real, non-symmetric semigroups that are contractive on a sector.

column6: Isolated singularities of weak solutions to the Serrin-critical $p$-Laplace equation
column7: We classify isolated singularities of nonnegative weak solutions to the Serrin-critical quasilinear Lane-Emden equation $-Δ_p u=u^{\frac{n(p-1)}{n-p}}$ in $B_1\setminus\{0\}$, where $1<p<n$, $Δ_p$ is the classical $p$-Laplacian operator and $B_1\setminus\{0\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is the punctured unit ball. We prove that either the origin is a removable singularity or $u$ satisfies $\lim_{x\to0}|x|^{\frac{n-p}{p-1}}(\log\frac1{|x|})^{\frac{n-p}{p(p-1)}}u(x)=[\frac{n-p}{p}(\frac{n-p}{p-1})^{p-1}]^{\frac{n-p}{p(p-1)}}$. This extends the result of Aviles (Comm. Math. Phys. 1987: 177--192) from the semilinear case $p=2$ to the full range $1<p<n$, without assuming radial symmetry. We develop a new BV-based argument for weak solutions. We also give a direct construction of positive radial singular solutions with the same asymptotic behavior.

column6: On the Complexity of Finding Stationary Points in Stochastic $(L_0, L_1)$-Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
column7: We study the stochastic first-order oracle (SFO) complexity of finding $ε$-stationary points of $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth nonconvex functions. Under bounded-variance noise, existing analyses of normalized and clipped stochastic gradient descent (SGD) establish optimal dependence on $ε$ and $L_0$, but the jointly optimal dependence on $L_0$, $L_1$, and $ε$ remains unclear. We resolve this question for an unbiased SFO whose gradient noise has a $p$th central moment bounded by $σ^p$ for some $σ\geq 0$, where $p\in(1,2]$.Specifically, we establish an SFO lower bound of $Ω\big(\big(σ^{\frac{p}{p-1}}ε^{-\frac{p}{p-1}}+1\big) (L_0 Δε^{-2}+L_1Δε^{-1})\big)$, where $Δ>0$ is the initial optimality gap.This bound identifies an unavoidable contribution proportional to $L_1ε^{-1}Δ$. We also prove that mini-batch (smoothed) normalized SGD can attain a matching upper bound, thereby establishing the optimal SFO complexity.

column6: Coprime pairs with equal sum of divisors, assuming smooth shifted primes
column7: Let $h(x)$ be the number of pairs $1\le a<b<x$ with $\gcd(a,b)=1$ and $σ(a)=σ(b)$. Erdős Problem #824 asks whether $h(x)>x^{2-o(1)}$. By an argument of Pollack and Pomerance, this follows if for every fixed $δ>0$ there are $y^{1-o(1)}$ primes $p\le5y$ with $p+1$ free of prime factors exceeding $y^δ$. We write this implication out with explicit parameters and formalize it in Lean 4. We then check that the argument of the recent OpenAI preprint "Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers", which claims the corresponding statement for $p-1$, applies to $p+1$ after a change of sign in two of its sections. Consequently $h(x)=x^{2-o(1)}$, conditionally on the correctness of that preprint, which has not been refereed and whose main new estimates we have not independently verified.

column6: Induced-Count Discrepancy in Uniform Hypergraphs
column7: Let $u_k^{(r)}(H,p)$ be the maximum, over all $k$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraphs $F$, of the absolute difference between the number of induced copies of $F$ in $H$ and its expectation in the binomial random $r$-graph with the same number of vertices as $H$ and edge probability $p$. Let $u_k^{(r)}(n,p)$ be the minimum of $u_k^{(r)}(H,p)$ over all $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraphs, and let $D_r(n,p)$ be the distance from $p\binom nr$ to the nearest integer. For fixed $r\ge3$, $k\ge2r$ and $\varepsilon>0$, the quantity $u_k^{(r)}(n,p)$ has order $\max\!\left\{D_r(n,p),p(1-p)\right\}n^{k-r}$ whenever $p(1-p)n^{\lfloor r/2\rfloor/(\binom{2r-2}{r}-1)}\ge\varepsilon$. Using local moment estimates and switchings in a sparse reservoir, we construct one hypergraph with the nearest-integer edge count that controls all induced orders simultaneously.

column6: When Do Restricted Sumsets Cover a Finite Abelian Group?
column7: For a subset $A$ of a finite abelian group $G$, let $Σ_k(A)$ denote the set of sums of $k$ distinct elements of $A$, and let $Σ(A)=\bigcup_{k\ge1}Σ_k(A)$. The problem of determining when $Σ(A)=G$ goes back to Erdős and Heilbronn. Nguyen and Vu later formulated the corresponding fixed-length question: for a prescribed $k$, when does $Σ_k(A)=G$? For groups of odd order, we prove the sharp large-order threshold $|A|>|G|/3+1$, which forces $Σ_k(A)=G$ throughout the entire middle range $4\le k\le |A|-4$. This determines the limiting thresholds posed by Girard, Griffiths and Hamidoune. If $p$ is the least prime divisor of $|G|$, then, for fixed odd $p$ and sufficiently large $|G|$, the exact threshold $|A|\ge |G|/p+p-1$ forces covering throughout the middle range beginning at $2p-2$. Thus, throughout this range, prescribing the number of summands does not change the sharp covering threshold. For $3\le k\le2p-3$, the restricted and ordinary $k$-fold covering problems have the same asymptotic threshold. As an application to MDS elliptic codes on an elliptic curve $E/\F_q$, we sharpen the half-scale conjecture of Li, Wan and Zhang, obtaining the sharp $1/3$-scale bound when $|E(\F_q)|$ is odd and, more generally, the exact bound determined by the least prime divisor of $|E(\F_q)|$.

column6: Besov spaces and product BMO over polydisc
column7: We prove that the analytic Besov space $B_{p,p}^{1/p}(\C_+^n)$ embeds continuously into Chang--Fefferman product BMO for every finite $n$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Consequently, every small Hankel operator in a finite Schatten class has a product BMO symbol. The proof uses smooth product wavelets and an estimate for dyadic rectangles. We also give a condition on Fejér means that yields a BMO symbol for a bounded Hankel operator on the polydisc.

column5: Valentina Ciccone; Mahdi Hormozi; José Madrid; Jakub Niksiński; Błażej Wróbel
column6: On $L^p$ norms of maximal operators
column7: We study the exact $L^p$ norms for a number of maximal operators, which are prominent in harmonic analysis, semigroup theory, and probability. We prove that a strongly continuous positive symmetric sub-Markovian semigroup $(T_t)_{t\ge0}$ on a nonatomic $σ$-finite measure space $(X,\mathcal F,μ)$ has maximal $L^p$ norm $p'=p/(p-1)$ for every $1<p<\infty$ whenever $f\mapsto T_{t_0}(\mathbf 1_Ef)$ is compact on $L^2(μ)$ for some $t_0>0$ and some measurable set $E$ of positive measure. The lower bound follows by approximating finite dyadic conditional expectations at suitable semigroup times; the upper bound is Stein's maximal inequality in its sub-Markovian form. Important examples of such maximal operators we discuss include maximal functions of various semigroups (heat, Poisson, Ornstein--Uhlenbeck, Schrödinger, Dunkl, Laguerre, Jacobi) as well as the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on $\mathbb{R}.$ In particular, the heat and Poisson maximal operators on every complete connected Riemannian manifold of positive dimension without boundary have exact $L^p$ norm $p'$, with no curvature or stochastic completeness assumptions. Combining our approach with previous work of the first and last authors we also prove that $p'$ is the limit, as $d\to \infty,$ of the $L^p$ norms $B(p,d)$ of the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operators on $\mathbb{R}^d.$ On the other hand, we show that the norm of this maximal operator is strictly larger than $p',$ in dimensions $d\ge2.$

column6: Sharp noncommutative Hilbert and Riesz inequalities: classification and spectral corrections
column7: For every $1<p<\infty$, with $p^*=\max\{p,p/(p-1)\}$, we determine the sharp Hilbert norm $C_p=\cot(π/(2p^*))$ on $L^p(\mathbb{R};\mathcal{S}_p)$ and the sharp uniform bound $D_p=\csc(π/p)$ for retained and strict Riesz projections of maximal subdiagonal algebras in finite tracial von Neumann algebras. The Hilbert value is also the common Fourier--Schur completely bounded norm. For finite matrices, a nonnegative logarithmic determinant defect connects Heinävaara's tracial joint spectral measure to eigenvalues. The resulting transfer identity classifies finite signed real ridge inequalities on nilpotents and identifies their least additive eigenvalue corrections. A dual theorem characterizes weak-* limits of weighted angular measures of finite nilpotents. In general finite tracial algebras, separate positive-kernel and sharp determinant-covariance comparisons yield the Riesz bounds. Consequences include the sharp Volterra constant, Riesz--Titchmarsh and shifted-transform formulas, joint real-pencil norms, and exact triangular and operator-valued Fourier Riesz norms.

column6: Sharp bounds and gap phenomena for large $p$-subgroups of automorphism groups of curves
column7: Let $X$ be a curve of genus $g\ge2$ over an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic $p$, and let $G=\mathrm{Aut}(X)$. A theorem of Giulietti and Korchmaros shows that if $G$ fixes no point and a $p$-subgroup $S\le G_P$ satisfies $|S|>\frac{p}{p-1}g$, then $X$ is one of the classical hyperelliptic, Hermitian, or Ree curves. We determine the sharp boundary and the first gap below it. At equality, besides the classical curves, exactly three types occur: the ordinary curves $y^p-y=x+c/x$, the zero-$p$-rank curves $y^3=x^p-x$ for $p\equiv2\pmod3$, and, in characteristic $3$, the ordinary genus-six family $y^3-y=c\left(x+\frac1{x^3-x}\right)$. As a key ingredient, we classify zero-$p$-rank curves whose full automorphism group fixes no point and which admit a $p$-subgroup of order larger than the genus. We then prove that, when $|S|>p$, the boundary classification already follows from the weaker inequality $|S|>p(g-p+1)/(p-1)$. For $|S|\ge p^3$, the forbidden interval above $m=(p-1)|S|/p$ has width at least $p(p-1)/2$, and below $m+(p^2-1)/2$ at most one further genus can occur, with a rigid ramification structure. Finally, we classify the first admissible layer: it occurs only for $|S|=p^2$, and the resulting ordinary curves admit a complete description in terms of two-dimensional Artin--Schreier spaces.

column6: Curvature, Scaling, and Complexity in Riemannian Projection-Free Optimization
column7: Projection-free methods replace projections by linear minimization oracles, making their convergence fundamentally sensitive to the geometry of the feasible region. We develop a geometric framework for this dependence in Riemannian Frank--Wolfe optimization. A power-type double-geodesic modulus quantifies the intrinsic geometry of the feasible set, and an exact transfer principle shows that this modulus induces a Frank--Wolfe scaling margin modulated by the differential of the Riemannian logarithm map. The resulting factorization separates the contributions of feasible-set geometry and ambient Riemannian distortion. Rauch comparison provides explicit curvature-dependent certificates for this distortion, while on the positive-definite cone equipped with the affine-invariant metric the logarithm differential admits an exact spectral characterization in terms of relative eigenvalue spread. Combined with a quadratic error bound, the power-type geometry yields the convergence rate $O(t^{-p/(p-1)})$ for the gap-feedback short-step policy. For every fixed $p>3$, a compact feasible set in a hyperbolic plane attains the matching rate $Θ(t^{-p/(p-1)})$ under the same policy. The geometry-derived exponent $p/(p-1)$ is therefore sharp for the gap-feedback short-step policy over the geometry-controlled class considered here.

column6: Tensor Envelopes in the Nonconvex Setting
column7: We introduce a tensor envelope (TEE) for composite objectives $\varphi=f+g$, built from a $q$th-order Taylor model of the smooth term $f$ regularized by a $p$th power with $p>q$. To construct it, we first establish a tensor descent lemma and characterize its behavior in the three regimes $q<p<q+1$, $p=q+1$, and $p>q+1$. Under suitable prox-boundedness and parameter conditions, the associated tensor operator (TOP) has nonempty compact values, and TEE is finite-valued and continuous, preserves global minimizers, and inherits the level-boundedness of $\varphi$. We further show that TEE is locally Lipschitz continuous and directionally differentiable, characterize its Fréchet differentiability, and prove that it is $C^1$ whenever TOP is single-valued. As such, TEE preserves the essential optimization landscape properties of $\varphi$ while enjoying a richer analytical structure, which facilitates the design and analysis of tensor-based optimization methods. Finally, TEE serves as a Lyapunov function for the exact tensor iteration: every cluster point is critical, and, for bounded trajectories with $q<p\le q+1$, an $ε$-stationary point is reached within $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-p/(p-1)})$ iterations. To our knowledge, both the tensor descent lemma and this complexity bound are the first of their kind obtained without assuming global Lipschitz or Hölder continuity of the $q$th-order derivative of $f$.

column6: Input-Endpoint Compactness and Essential Norms for Weighted Bilinear Hardy Operators
column7: We study compactness of the product of two weighted Hardy primitives into $L^q(u)$, $0<q<\infty$, on the input boundary $1\le p_1,p_2\le\infty$, where at least one input exponent is $1$ or $\infty$. For $L^1\times L^p$, $1<p<\infty$, boundedness implies compactness when $q<p/(p+1)$. For $L^1\times L^1$, the corresponding range is $q<1/2$. At and above these boundaries compactness is characterized by additional active-tail decay, and critical power weights give bounded noncompact examples. The endpoint reductions use cumulative Stieltjes measures with their initial atoms and strict Hardy-Copson brackets. An output-mass allocation argument proves local finite-rank density, including quasi-Banach targets. Applying the localization principles developed for the interior-input regime identifies the essential distance, finite-rank distance and Hausdorff noncompactness radius with the coupled active tail, with the appropriate metric power when $q<1$. For a finite left endpoint, ordinary $L^\infty$ inputs admit an exact scalar transfer completed by linear nodal approximation.

column6: Singer-Difference-Set Qudit Stabilizer Codes from Non-Degenerate Quadrics in PG(d,q)PG(d,q): Construction, Structural Theorems, and Monte-Carlo Performance
column7: We propose Q(q,d), a family of q-ary non-CSS qudit stabilizer codes with prime power q and dimension d >= 2, constructed from Singer difference sets and non-degenerate quadrics in PG(d,q). The parity check H = (A | M_Q A) couples the Singer-circulant incidence matrix A with the quadric circulant M_Q, and a Cancellation Lemma uses the identity (k - lambda) = q^{d-1} = 0 mod p to make H symplectic-isotropic over F_q. Five structural theorems carry the novelty: a cross-correlation modular-constancy identity nu = 1 mod q at q odd, d >= 3, with a two-value pattern that proves a 2-torsion distance ceiling; a CRT zero-count identity; an explicit Clifford bridge identifying Q(q,2) as a graph-state encoding of the trivial Singer CSS code, with the 2021 low-density-spreading (LDS) sign-flip pattern realised by a symmetric circulant; a paired column-rigidity equality d_min = R_P + 1; and a lower bound d_min(Q(7,2)) >= 8 from an exhaustive Singer-Frobenius search. A Hamada-Smith specialisation yields the closed-form logical dimension k(p,d) = theta_d(p) - C(p+d-1, d) - 1, and the flagship Q(p,2) = [[p^2 + p + 1, p(p+1)/2, d_min]]_p attains asymptotic rate one-half. We conjecture d_min(Q(p,2)) = p + 1 for odd primes, proven at p = 5 and lower-bounded to >= 8 at p = 7. Instances include Q(3,2) = [[13,6,3]]_3, Q(5,2) = [[31,15,6]]_5, Q(7,2) = [[57,28, d>=8]]_7, and Q(3,4) = [[121,105,3]]_3. Monte-Carlo over 1.5 x 10^6 trials shows Q(5,2) achieves a 70-fold per-logical-qudit improvement over Steane [[7,1,3]]_2 at depolarising rate 10^-3 with zero silent logical errors. A textbook bounded-distance decoder is used; Berlekamp-Massey-style cyclic decoding is left as the natural sequel.

column6: Phase transition, sharp asymptotics and symmetry for critical quasilinear Hartree equations beyond $σ=2p$
column7: We establish the sharp asymptotic and symmetry theory for the critical quasilinear Hartree equation \[ -Δ_pu=\big(|x|^{-σ}*u^{p^*_σ}\big)u^{p^*_σ-1} \quad\text{in }\mathbb R^N, \qquad p^*_σ=\frac{p(2N-σ)}{2(N-p)}, \] in the complementary range $2p<σ<N$, beyond the quasilinear theory previously available for $σ\le2p$ [Math. Ann., 391(2):2653--2708, 2025]. This range is structurally different: $p^*_σ<p$, so the effective potential obtained by factoring out $u^{p-1}$ becomes singular as $u\to0$. Nevertheless, whenever $p^*_σ>1$, every nonnegative finite-energy weak solution is automatically locally bounded. Our proof provides a quasilinear regularity mechanism adapted to this complementary range, where the potential-theoretic route available for $σ\le2p$ breaks down. For positive finite-energy solutions with $p^*_σ>1$ we moreover uncover a sharp transition governed by the sign of $σ(p-2)+2p$. If this quantity is positive, the classical $p$-harmonic profile persists. At the threshold, \[ u(x)\simeq |x|^{-γ_h}(\log|x|)^{1/(p-p^*_σ)}, \qquad γ_h=\frac{N-p}{p-1}, \] with the matching two-sided gradient rate. Below the threshold, \[ u(x)=A_*|x|^{-γ_*}+o(|x|^{-γ_*}), \qquad γ_*=\frac{2(N-p)(σ-p)}{p(σ-2p)}<γ_h, \] and the rescaled gradients converge uniformly to the corresponding radial profile. In all three regimes the solutions are radially symmetric about some point and strictly decreasing in the radial variable.

column6: On the largest prime factors of $p-1$ and $p+1$
column7: We prove that each of the inequalities $P^{+}(p+1)>P^{+}(p-1)$ and $P^{+}(p-1)>P^{+}(p+1)$ holds for a positive proportion of primes. The argument combines a logarithmic balance identity with a uniform Selberg sieve over a thin cofactor strip. The same transfer mechanism applies to either shift and converts a one-sided large-prime-factor reservoir into an unconditional ordering result in both directions.

column5: Fan Bu; Dachun Yang; Wen Yuan
column6: Sharp Matrix-Weighted Lower Bounds for Non-Degenerate Convolution Calderón--Zygmund Operators
column7: Let $T$ be a convolution Calderón--Zygmund operator satisfying Hytönen's non-degeneracy condition. We prove that, for every $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $m\ge3$, there exists a positive constant $C$ such that, for any $t\in[1,\infty)$, \begin{equation*} \sup_{[W]_{\mathcal A_p}\le t} \|T\|_{L^p(W)\to L^p(W)} \ge C t^{1+\frac{1}{p(p-1)}}, \end{equation*} where the supremum is taken over all matrix weights $W:\ \mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C^{m\times m}$ with their weight constants $[W]_{\mathcal A_p}\le t$. If, in addition, the odd part of the kernel is non-degenerate (such as the Hilbert transform and the Riesz transforms), the same conclusion holds for every $m\ge2$.

column6: Nontransitivity of braid group actions on exceptional bases in $K_0(\mathbb{P}^n)$ for $n=4,6$
column7: Let $X=\mathbb{P}^n$, where $p=n+1$ is prime. Consider the orbit of the standard numerical exceptional basis in $K_0(X)$ under mutations, sign changes, and isometries of the Euler form. We construct an invariant of this orbit: for every basis from the orbit, the square of rank of all basic vectors art congruent to $1$ modulo $p$. For $\mathbb{P}^4$ and $\mathbb{P}^6$, we present explicit numerical exceptional bases violating this congruence; hence the action is not transitive. We also establish a stronger obstruction modulo $p^2$ and use Polishchuk's theorem to show that no vector of the constructed bases is the class of an exceptional object. Finally, we prove that for every prime $p$, the category $D^b(\operatorname{Coh}\mathbb{P}^{p-1}_{\mathbb C})$ does not contain a pair of mutually orthogonal exceptional objects.

column6: The weak type $(1,1)$ estimate of Dirichlet Means for unbounded noncommutative Vilenkin systems
column7: Let $\mathcal{R}$ be the hyperfinite $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor. Considering the partial sum operators $(\mathcal{S}_n)_{n\geq 1}$ of the noncommutative Vilenkin-Fourier series associated with an arbitrary admissible Vilenkin group, we prove that there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that \begin{equation*} \sup_{n\geq1}\|\mathcal{S}_n(f)\|_{L_{1,\infty}(\mathcal{R})} \leq c\|f\|_{L_1(\mathcal{R})},\quad f \in L_1(\mathcal{R}), \end{equation*} and, for every $1<p<\infty$, $$\sup_{n\geq1}\|\mathcal{S}_n(f)\|_{L_p(\mathcal{R})} \leq c\frac{p}{p-1}\|f\|_{L_p(\mathcal{R})},\quad f \in L_p(\mathcal{R}).$$ Besides the transference technique, the main novel ingredient is a modified version of noncommutative Calderón-Zygmund decomposition established in \cite{CCP2022}. Consequently, we resolve the problem of weak type $(1,1)$ estimate communicated to the authors by Fedor Sukochev, and substantially improve the strong type (p,p) estimates obtained in \cite{DFdePS2001} by achieving the optimal order $\frac{p}{p-1}$.

column6: The planar Calderón problem for $L^p$ potentials
column7: We prove that the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map associated to the Schrödinger operator $-Δ+q$ on a planar bounded Lipschitz domain uniquely determines an arbitrary complex-valued potential $q\in L^p$, $p>1$, whenever zero is not a Dirichlet eigenvalue. Our argument uses Nachman's d-bar equation only at sufficiently large complex frequencies, where exceptional points are absent. A new annular frequency estimate converts the first asymptotic coefficient of the complex geometric optics solutions into a pointwise bound for a primitive of the potential difference, reducing the inverse problem to a unique-continuation argument.

column5: Chen Wang; Xiaoyan Zhang; Chunming Tang; Zhengchun Zhou
column6: Explicit Constructions of Maximum-Cardinality Families of Plateaued Functions with Pairwise Disjoint Walsh Supports
column7: Families of plateaued Boolean functions with pairwise disjoint Walsh supports are useful in secondary constructions of cryptographic Boolean functions. Of particular interest are maximum-cardinality families whose members admit no nonzero linear structures. To the best of our knowledge, the previously known general construction attaining both properties is spectral (Hodžić et al., IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 65(9): 5865--5879, 2019). In that work, explicit algebraic normal forms are not generally provided, and no general method is established for prescribing a common algebraic degree for all family members. In this paper, we present two new explicit algebraic constructions within a unified framework, one based on linear functions and the other on partially linear functions with bent components. Let $p\geq 2$ and $q\geq 0$ satisfy $q<2^p-p-1$, and set $m=p+q$. Both constructions yield maximum-cardinality families of $2^{q+1}$ $(q+1)$-plateaued Boolean functions with pairwise disjoint Walsh supports. No member admits a nonzero linear structure, and every member has an explicit generalized Maiorana--McFarland representation. The first construction produces functions in $m+p+1$ variables and realizes any prescribed common algebraic degree $3\leq d\leq p+1$, provided that $q<\sum_{i=2}^{d-1}\binom{p}{i}$; its maximum attainable degree $p+1$ is optimal. The second construction produces functions in $n+p+1$ variables, where $n>m$ and $n-m$ is even, and realizes any prescribed common algebraic degree $3\leq d\leq p+(n-m)/2$, provided that $q<\sum_{i=2}^{\min\{d-1,p\}}\binom{p}{i}$; its maximum attainable degree $p+(n-m)/2$ is next-to-optimal.

column6: Complete mapping criteria for generalized Cesàro operators between Hardy spaces
column7: Let $μ$ be a finite positive Borel measure on $[0,1)$ and let $γ>0$. We establish sharp mapping criteria for the generalized Cesàro operator \begin{equation*} \mathcal C_{μ,γ}f(z) =\sum_{n=0}^\infty μ_n \left(\sum_{k=0}^n \frac{Γ(n-k+γ)}{Γ(γ)(n-k)!}a_k\right)z^n,\qquad z\in \mathbb{D},\end{equation*} between Hardy spaces, including the source and target $H^\infty$ endpoints. For $0<p<q<\infty$, for $0<p=q<1$, and for $0<p\le1$ with $q=\infty$, the boundedness of $ \mathcal C_{μ,γ}: H^p \to H^q$ is equivalent to $μ$ being a $(γ+1/p-1/q)$-Carleson measure, without further restrictions on $γ$. For $1\le q<p\le\infty$, set $1/r=1/q-1/p$. In this range, boundedness and compactness are equivalent to \[ \int_0^1 \left(\frac{μ([t,1))}{(1-t)^{γ-1/r}}\right)^r \frac{dt}{1-t}<\infty. \] This condition is also equivalent to $F_{μ,γ}\in H^r$ and to $\sum_{n\ge0}(n+1)^{rγ-2}μ_n^r<\infty$, where $F_{μ,α}=\mathcal C_{μ,α}(1)$ and $μ_n=\int_{[0,1)}t^n\,dμ(t)$. For $1<p<\infty$, boundedness and compactness from $H^p$ to $H^\infty$ are characterized by the shifted condition $F_{μ,γ+1}\in H^{p'}$, where $p'=p/(p-1)$. We therefore obtain a complete boundedness classification of the generalized Cesàro operators $\mathcal C_{μ,γ}$ between Hardy spaces $H^p$ and $H^q$ for the full range $0<p,q\le\infty$.

column6: A Lorentz Endpoint and Quantitative Obstruction for a Cowling-Price Moment Reduction
column7: Let $$ M_{r,p}^{(d)}(g)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}|x|^r|g(x)|^p\,dx, \qquad 1<p<\infty. $$ Write $p'=p/(p-1)$ and $ω_d=|B(0,1)|$. A direct step in the Wigderson--Wigderson moment method asks for a single-function estimate $$ \lVert g\rVert_1\le K\lVert g\rVert_q^{\,1-pη} \bigl(M_{r,p}^{(d)}(g)\bigr)^η, \qquad η=\frac{d(1-1/q)}{r+d-dp/q}. $$ We give a self-contained proof that, in its scale-invariant regime, this estimate holds exactly when $r>d(p-1)$. We then quantify the transition: the best constant blows up like $[r-d(p-1)]^{-1/p'}$ at the critical line, while on the annulus $1\le |x|\le R$ the endpoint loss is exactly $(dω_d\log R)^{1/p'}$. The critical line nevertheless has two sharp Lorentz endpoints. The strong moment controls $L^{1,p}$, $$ \lVert g\rVert_{L^{1,p}}\le ω_d^{1/p'}M_{d(p-1),p}^{(d)}(g)^{1/p}, $$ and strengthening the weighted norm from $L^p$ to $L^{p,1}$ restores the strong target, $$ \lVert g\rVert_1\le ω_d^{1/p'} \lVert |x|^{d/p'}g\rVert_{L^{p,1}}. $$ More generally, every power moment has a sharp target Lorentz space, and its secondary index is optimal. These results identify the endpoint lost by the direct same-$q$ reduction. They do not obstruct auxiliary-norm versions of the Wigderson framework, which reach the Cowling--Price range by a different route.

column6: Gabor Frame Regions and Non-Frame Obstructions for an even Rational Window
column7: We study the Gabor frame properties of the rational window $$ g(x)=\frac{x^2-1}{(x^2+1)(x^2+4)(x^2+9)}, $$ whose poles occur in symmetric pairs. We prove that every lattice satisfying $0<αβ<1/3$ generates a frame, and we establish an additional frame region for $β\ge1$ and $1/3\le αβ<0.47373$. Furthermore, we show that the rational hyperbolas $αβ=\frac{p}{3p-1}$, for $p\ge2,$ are entirely contained within the frame set. In contrast, we construct explicit non-frame lattice points on the hyperbolas $$αβ\in\left\{\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{2},\frac{2}{3},\frac{3}{4}\right\}.$$ Finally, for the density family $αβ=p/(p+1)$, we derive a symmetry reduction of the associated Zibulski-Zeevi matrix, providing numerical evidence for a richer structure of non-frame obstructions.

column6: New sharp lifespan estimates for a semilinear heat equation with zero-mass sign-changing initial data
column7: We consider the Cauchy problem $$u_t-Δu=|u|^p,\qquad (t,x)\in(0,T)\times\R^n, \quad u(0,x)=\eps u_0(x),\qquad x\in\R^n,$$ with small sign-changing initial data having zero total mass. We assume $$u_0\in L^1(\R^n)\cap L^\infty(\R^n),\quad |x|u_0\in L^1(\R^n),\quad \int_{\R^n}u_0(x)\,dx=0,$$ and, for the sharp subcritical upper bounds, that $\int_{\R^n}x\,u_0(x)\,dx\neq0.$ Let $T_\eps$ denote the maximal lifespan. We identify a new transition exponent $p_m=1+\frac1{n+1}$ inside the Fujita range $1<p\le p_F:=1+2/n$, and establish the sharp lifespan estimates $$T_\eps\asymp \begin{cases} \eps^{-\frac{2(p-1)}{2-(n+1)(p-1)}}, &1<p<p_m,\\[2mm] \eps^{-\frac2{n+1}} \bigl(\log\frac1\eps\bigr)^{-\frac2{n+2}}, &p=p_m,\\[2mm] \eps^{-p\left(\frac{1}{p-1}-\frac{n}{2}\right)^{-1}}, &p_m<p<p_F,\\[2mm] \exp\!\left(\eps^{-p(p-1)}\right), & p=p_F. \end{cases}$$ These estimates reveal a lifespan phenomenon that is different from the classical Lee--Ni law for initial data with positive mass. In the zero-mass setting, the leading linear contribution is dipole-like, while the nonlinear source subsequently generates a positive mass of size \(O(\eps^p)\). Their competition produces the additional threshold \(p_m\), the logarithmic correction at $p=p_m$, and, at $p=p_F$, a substantially longer critical lifespan with exponent $p_F(p_F-1)$ instead of the classical Lee--Ni exponent $p_F-1$. The upper estimates are obtained by backward-Gaussian and critical scale-ODE test-function arguments, whereas the lower estimates follow from a unified $L^1$--$L^\infty$ bootstrap preserving the zero-mass cancellation of the linear flow and controlling the mass generated by the nonlinear source. Thus, although $p_F$ remains the Fujita critical exponent, zero initial mass creates a new quantitative lifespan regime below and at the critical exponent.

column6: On the largest prime factors less than $y$ of consecutive shifted primes
column7: For an integer $n > 1$, let $P^+(n)$ be the largest prime factor of $n$, and let $P_y^+(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$ not exceeding $y$. One of Erdős and Turán's conjectures asserts that the asymptotic density of integers $n$ satisfying $P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)$ is $1/2$. Furthermore, Wang conjectures that for $x\rightarrow\infty$, one has $\#\{p\leq x:P^+(p-1)<P^+(p+1)\}\sim π(x)/2$. In this paper, we show the following results. For any $3\leq y\ll x^{o(1)}$, for $x\rightarrow\infty$, we have \begin{align*} &\#\{n\leq x:P^+_y(n)<P^+_y(n+1)\}\sim \frac{1}{2}x, \\&\#\{p\leq x:P^+_y(p-1)<P^+_y(p+1)\}\sim \frac{1}{2}π(x), \end{align*} where the first result extends a previous range $3\leq y\ll \exp(\log x/(100\log\log x))$ due to Rivat (2001). For any $0<α<17/32$, let $y=x^α$. Then there exists $h(α)>0$ such that \begin{align*} \#\{p\leq x:P_y^+(p-1)<P_y^+(p+1)\}\geq(h(α)+o(1))π(x). \end{align*} In particular, the function $h$ satisfies $\lim_{α\rightarrow 0^+}h(α)=1/2$. Similar result also holds for $\#\{n\leq x:P_y^+(n)<P_y^+(n+1)\}$, which improves a previous result $\lim_{α\rightarrow 0^+} h(α)=1/4$ due to Wang (2019).

column5: Yong Jiao; Xingyan Quan; Lian Wu; Guangheng Xie
column6: On the matrix $A_p$ conjecture
column7: This paper provides a solution to the matrix $A_p$ conjecture. For every \(1<p<\infty\), we construct a family of \(2\times2\) matrix \(A_p\) weights $W$ with arbitrarily large characteristics for which \[\|H\|_{L^p(W)\to L^p(W)}\ge c_p[W]_{A_p}^{1+1/[p(p-1)]},\] where \(H\) is the Hilbert transform and \(c_p>0\) depends only on \(p\).

column5: Hau Chan; Jianan Lin; Chenhao Wang
column6: Learning-Augmented Strategyproof Facility Location in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $\ell_p$ Distances
column7: We study learning-augmented mechanism design for locating a single facility in $\mathbb{R}^d$ to minimize the sum of the agents' $\ell_p$ distances to the facility. We analyze the coordinate-wise median with predictions (CMP) mechanism, which adds $cn$ virtual agents at a predicted optimal facility location to the $n$ reported locations and returns their coordinate-wise median. The parameter $c\in[0,1)$ represents confidence in the prediction; CMP is known to be strategyproof when both are fixed independently of the reports. We determine its approximation guarantees under correct predictions (consistency) and arbitrary predictions (robustness) in two settings. First, for $d=2$, we establish exact guarantees for every $p\in[1,+\infty]$. For $1<p<+\infty$, the consistency and robustness are respectively $\Bigl(1+\bigl(\frac{1-c}{1+c}\bigr)^{\frac{p}{p-1}}\Bigr)^{\frac{p-1}{p}}$ and $\Bigl(1+\bigl(\frac{1+c}{1-c}\bigr)^{\frac{p}{p-1}}\Bigr)^{\frac{p-1}{p}}$. We use the median condition in each coordinate to compare the mechanism's cost with the optimal cost, and establish tightness using instances with agents at only three distinct locations. Second, for $1<p<+\infty$, we obtain dimension-independent consistency and robustness upper bounds valid for every $d\ge1$. For each fixed $p$ and $c$, we construct families of instances whose ratios approach the respective upper bounds as $d\to\infty$, proving asymptotic tightness. We also establish exact guarantees for $p=1$ in every dimension and asymptotically tight bounds for $p=+\infty$. Our high-dimensional results recover the prediction-free bounds of Gravin and Jia (STOC 2025) when $c=0$ and their learning-augmented bounds in arbitrary-dimensional Euclidean spaces when $p=2$.

column6: Moments Comparison Inequalities for Critical 2d Stochastic Heat Flow, Polymers and GMC
column7: We employ a Gaussian convex inequality developed in [AC15], [Che26], [Gue22], and [FUMPC26] to establish (one sided) moment comparison inequalities for Gaussian multiplicative chaos, directed polymers in Gaussian environment and, in particular, the Critical 2d Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF), including upper bounds on negative moments, as well as similar lower bounds for $p$-th moments with $p\in (0,1)$. For the Critical 2d SHF, averaged over small balls, we also obtain the matching (up to multiplicative constants) complementary bounds. We establish the complementary bounds using a bootstrap argument inspired by [DS10] and a geometric decomposition introduced in [GT26]. Specifically, we prove that for locally averaged SHF, for every $p\in\mathbb R$, the $p$-th moment is, up to multiplicative constants, bounded in both sides by the $\frac{p(p-1)}{2}$-th power of its second moment.

column6: The norm of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator
column7: We determine the exact $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ norm of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator for every $1<p<\infty$, proving that it equals $p/(p-1)$. This settles the sharp strong-type problem for the centered maximal operator on the real line. For every $p$ in this range, the norm is strictly larger than the constant associated with the critical power $|x|^{-1/p}$, thereby disproving the conjecture of Dror, Ganguli, and Strichartz that this profile determines the unrestricted norm.

column6: Radial solutions of quasilinear Hardy--Emden--Fowler equations: exact decay rates, Delaunay solutions, and nonexistence
column7: Let $N>p>1$, $s>-p$, $0<μ<\barμ:=\big(\frac{N-p}{p}\big)^{p}$ and $q>p-1$. We determine the behaviour at infinity of \emph{every} positive solution of the quasilinear Hardy--Emden--Fowler equation \[ -\big(r^{N-1}|v'|^{p-2}v'\big)'=μ\,r^{N-1-p}v^{p-1}+r^{N-1+s}v^{q}, \qquad r>R_{0}. \] Three rates compete: the self-similar rate $r^{-γ_{*}}$ with $γ_{*}=\frac{p+s}{q-p+1}$, and the two Hardy rates $r^{-ν_{\pm}}$, where $ν_{\pm}$ are the roots of $h(ν):=ν^{p-1}(N-p-(p-1)ν)=μ$. Writing $p^{*}_{s}=\frac{p(N+s)}{N-p}$ and $q_{S}=p-1+\frac{p+s}{ν_{+}}$ for the Hardy--Sobolev and Serrin exponents, we obtain a complete picture in four regimes. If $q>p^{*}_{s}-1$, every solution realises exactly one of the three rates, with a logarithmic correction in the borderline case $h(γ_{*})=μ$, and we compute the leading constants. If $q=p^{*}_{s}-1$ the system becomes integrable: besides the singular self-similar solution and a heteroclinic ``bubble'' there is a one-parameter family of Fowler--Delaunay solutions, for which $r^{γ_{*}}v(r)$ is a non-constant periodic function of $\ln r$. If $q_{S}<q<p^{*}_{s}-1$ only two orbits survive, and if $q\le q_{S}$ there is no positive solution at all in an exterior domain. This is the quasilinear, weighted counterpart of the picture obtained by Franca and Sfecci for $p=2$. We work with the slope variables $x=-rv'/v$, $Y=r^{p+s}v^{q-p+1}$, in which the equation becomes a planar system that is real-analytic on the half-plane $\{x>0\}$ for every $1<p<N$, so that no restriction of the type $p\le2$ is needed; the analysis then rests on a universal barrier $x<ν_{+}$, on an explicit Dulac function which degenerates into a first integral exactly at $q=p^{*}_{s}-1$, and on an explicit Lyapunov function.

column5: Hong-Lin Liu; Zhong-Wen Feng; Qing-Quan Jiang; Xia Zhou; Xue-Ling Mu
column6: Matter-induced global regularity in non-polynomial quasi-topological gravity with Born-Infeld electrodynamics
column7: We construct exact static, spherically symmetric charged solutions in four-dimensional non-polynomial quasi-topological gravity coupled to Born-Infeld electrodynamics. We focus on the model $h(p)=p/(1+\ell^{2}p)$, whose vacuum branch develops a curvature singularity at a finite radius. We show that Born-Infeld nonlinearities can remove this singularity within a finite region of parameter space, yielding globally regular geometries with an asymptotically flat exterior and a finite-curvature AdS-type core. The regular sector contains both horizonless configurations and RBHs, separated by a degenerate-horizon boundary. We further identify a continuous branch of regular black holes with a triple-degenerate inner horizon and a simple outer event horizon, satisfying $κ_-=0$ and $κ_+\neq0$. These results provide a converse example to cases in which introducing charge spoils the regularity of a black hole that is regular in vacuum. In the present model, Born-Infeld electrodynamics instead removes the finite-radius singularity of a gravitational branch that is singular in vacuum and supports globally regular charged geometries, including regular black holes with nontrivial inner-horizon structure.

column5: Thai-Son Vu; Hoang-Giang Nguyen; Quoc-Bao Nguyen; Sengaloun Keoalounxay; Bao-Viet Tran
column6: Reciprocity can halve what a mechanical network can learn
column7: A passive, reciprocal, linear network driven by forces or currents and read at points it drives cannot be trained below an error floor computed from the target beforehand. The usual parameter count for such networks does not charge for Maxwell-Betti reciprocity. We prove that when such an elastic, resistor or flow network has a symmetric response operator and p driven degrees of freedom are also read, its reachable response blocks lie in a subspace of codimension p(p-1)/2, whatever its size and topology, and the floor is the distance to it. On targets with a reachable symmetric part, a second-order optimiser ends within 0.1% of the floor in 142 of 144 simulated runs, and a contrastive rule with a bond-local update direction, within its step budget, in 22 of 24. Reciprocity charges a list of single drive-read tasks only for the pairs it instruments in both directions, and a rank test on the passive network says in advance whether, and on which bonds, odd couplings locally restore the lost directions, at a cost in non-reciprocity that the target bounds from below. Under an imposed-displacement drive, the one most physical-learning hardware uses, reciprocity survives as a weaker law, an exact balance between forward and reverse transmissions once each is weighted by the driving-point compliance at its input, and an inequality on their product, under which no symmetric positive-definite chain meets both targets of a published robotic metamaterial. All nineteen published layouts we tabulated pay nothing; a force-driven layout that asks one pair to respond differently in its two directions will.

column6: Consensus time for asynchronous $\ell^p$ relaxation: graph dependence
column7: We study the asynchronous $\ell^p$ relaxation introduced by Amir, Nazarov, and Peres: at each step, a uniformly chosen vertex minimizes its incident $\ell^p$ energy. For the profile $f_t$ after $t$ updates, let $$ \mathsf T_p(G,1/2):= \sup_{\lVert f_0\rVert_\infty\le1} \mathbb{E}\bigl[\min\{t\ge0:\operatorname{osc}(f_t)\le1/2\}\bigr]. $$ For $1<p<\infty$, we obtain graph-dependent estimates for boxes, trees, and conductance expanders. On the nearest-neighbor box $[L]^d$, for $d,L\ge2$ and $n=L^d$, the answer is, up to logarithmic factors, $nd^{1/(p-1)}L^{p/(p-1)}$ for $1<p<2$ and $ndL^2$ for $p\ge2$. On bounded-degree trees, an explicit rerooting-invariant parameter $T_G$ determines the answer up to logarithmic factors; for arbitrary trees it gives upper and lower bounds that differ additionally by the maximum degree. If the volume conductance $h(G)\ge h_0>0$, then $\mathsf T_p(G,1/2)=Θ_{p,h_0}(n\log n)$ without a degree assumption. At $p=\infty$, every connected graph satisfies $\mathsf T_\infty(G,1/2)\ge c nD^2/Δ$, where $D$ and $Δ$ are its diameter and maximum degree.

column6: Conservation of mass for solutions of Leibenson's equation on Riemannian Manifolds
column7: We consider on a Riemannian manifold $M$ the Leibenson equation \begin{equation*}\label{eqabs}\partial _{t}u=Δ_{p}u^{q},\end{equation*} where $p>1$ and $q>0$. When $q(p-1)\geq 1$, we prove conservation of mass for solutions of Leibenson's equation assuming only the volume bound $V(x_0, r)\leq \exp\left(C r^{\frac{p}{p-1}}\right)$ for some $x_{0}\in M$ and all large enough $r>0$. When $q(p-1)< 1$, we prove this property assuming $V(x_0, r)\leq Cr^{N}$ and $p>N[1-q(p-1)]$, which matches the threshold in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ with $N=n$. We also show that solutions on the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n}$ have a finite extinction time in the case $q(p-1)< 1$, which implies that the conservation of mass property does not hold. Using the conservation of mass result in the case $q(p-1)=1$, we also prove a $L^{p-1}$- Liouville property, which partially answers a conjecture stated by I. Holopainen \cite{holopainen2000sharp}.

column6: The complete spectrum of the linearized $p$-Laplacian at a Sobolev extremal
column7: Let $1<p<n$ and let $v(x)=(1+|x|^{p/(p-1)})^{-(n-p)/p}$ be the standard radial extremal for the sharp Sobolev inequality. We determine all eigenvalues and eigenspaces of the linearized $p$-Laplacian at $v$, defined by its closed quadratic form in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n,v^{p^*-2} dx)$. After decomposition into spherical harmonics, an explicit gauge transformation and a change of variables identify each radial operator with a shifted Jacobi operator. This yields a complete eigenbasis indexed by $(\ell,k)\in\mathbb{N}_0^2$, where $\ell$ is the angular degree and $k$ is the radial mode number.

column6: Connecting Riemannian Geometry and Statistical Inference for Correlation Matrices
column7: The quotient-affine metric gives an intrinsic Riemannian geometry to full-rank correlation matrices, but its geodesic distance has no closed form and we are not aware of an analytic asymptotic null distribution for it. We connect this geometry, introduced in 2019, with Jennrich's 1970 asymptotic test for equality of correlation matrices. The quadratic form underlying Jennrich's statistic is exactly one half of the quotient-affine metric tensor. The identity arises because eliminating marginal standard deviations from Gaussian Fisher information performs the same projection as quotienting out diagonal rescalings. Jennrich's statistic therefore evaluates the local quotient-affine quadratic form directly. Moreover, for two independent Gaussian samples with a common population correlation matrix, the squared geodesic distance, scaled by effective sample size, converges in distribution to $4χ^2_d$, where $d = p(p-1)/2$. For $p=2$, the result reduces to the two-sample Fisher $z$ test.

column5: Tan Duc Do; Nguyen Ngoc Trong; Nguyen Ngoc Huy Truong
column6: A Weighted Bossel-Daners Transfer Principle and a Pure-Power Robin Faber-Krahn Inequality
column7: We prove a weighted Bossel-Daners transfer principle for the first Robin eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian under $w=m^{1/p'}$, where $p'=p/(p-1)$. The argument combines double-density isoperimetry with spectral admissibility for singular weights and normalized-flux monotonicity. It uses an exact $BV$ zero-extension formula, an $L^{p'}(m\,dx)$ selection lemma, and a nonatomic rank map that remains well defined on positive-measure level sets. For the singular pair \[ m_b(x)=|x|^b, \qquad w_b(x)=|x|^{b/p'}, \] known power-weight isoperimetry provides the geometric input. We establish spectral admissibility up to the critical exponent $p=N$ and, for the positive radial first eigenfunction $z=z(r)$ on the centered ball $B_R$, derive the integrated singular radial equation and center asymptotics and prove directly that \[ θ_R'(r)>0 \quad(0<r<R), \qquad θ_R(r)=\frac{|z'(r)|^{p-1}}{r^{b/p'}z(r)^{p-1}}, \] with $θ_R(0)=0$ and $θ_R(R)=β$. Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a finite union of bounded connected Lipschitz domains whose closures are pairwise disjoint, let $Ω_b^\sharp$ be the centered ball of equal $|x|^b$-weighted volume, and let $λ_{1,β}^b$ denote the first eigenvalue for the displayed pair. Consequently, \[ λ_{1,β}^{b}(Ω_b^\sharp) \le λ_{1,β}^{b}(Ω) \] whenever $N\ge 2$, $1<p\le N$, $-p<b<0$, and $β>0$. The range $1<p<N$ is complementary to the previously known $p\ge N$ weighted Talenti theory; at the shared endpoint $p=N$, the present proof also permits the singular contact $0\in\partialΩ$.

column6: Sharp Quasi-Reverse Minkowski Inequality for Schatten Norms
column7: Let $\|\cdot\|_p$ denote the Schatten $p$-norm and let $|A|=(A^*A)^{1/2}$. For $2\leq p<\infty$, let $x_{p,m}>1$ be the unique solution of $x_{p,m}^p=2x_{p,m}+m-1$, and set \[ C_{p,m}=\frac{\sqrt{x_{p,m}(x_{p,m}+m-1)}}{(x_{p,m}^p+m-1)^{1/p}}. \] We prove the sharp inequality \[ \|A_1+\cdots+A_m\|_p\leq C_{p,m}\bigl\||A_1|+\cdots+|A_m|\bigr\|_p \] for arbitrary complex matrices of arbitrary size. Equivalently, if $q=p/(p-1)$ and $R,X_1,\cdots,+X_m$ are positive semidefinite, then \[ \|RX_1\|_1+\cdots\|RX_m\|_1 \leq C_{p,m}\|R\|_q\|X_1+\cdots X_m\|_p. \] For $1<p<2$, we also show that the formula proposed for the optimal constant fails. We give both a numerical counterexample and a systematic analytic construction.oposed for the optimal constant fails. We give both a numerical counterexample and a systematic analytic construction.

column6: Organizing transitions and their cascades: Generalized symmetry enforcement in massless flows or Higgs transitions
column7: We study the role of generalized symmetry in massless renormalization group flows or Higgs transitions. In particular, we revisit the massless renormalization group flows in unitary minimal models, $\mathbf{M}(p,p+1) \rightarrow \overline{\mathbf{M}(p-1,p)}$ preserving the fusion ring symmetry $\text{FR} (SU(2)_{p-2})\subset \mathbf{M}(p,p+1)$ where $p$ is an integer satisfying $p>3$. In this series of flows, we demonstrate that the unbroken fusion ring symmetry $\text{FR} (SU(2)_{p-2})$ eliminates all relevant perturbations in the $\overline{\mathbf{M}(p-1,p)}$ model. Hence, the infrared theory $\overline{\mathbf{M}(p-1,p)}$ is stable at the level of the scaling analysis and can be interpreted as a (weak-)symmetry-enforced gapless phase in contemporary theoretical physics. Phenomenologically, by the folding trick, the unbroken fusion ring symmetry corresponds to a (half-)integer spin nonsimple current, a variant of the Cooper pair involving nonabelian anyons generated from the coset or level-rank duality structures. Moreover, we demonstrate that the structure of (half-)integer spin nonsimple current plays a fundamental role in causing the resonance effect of relevant and dangerously irrelevant perturbations. This resonance effect may result in the cascade of phase transitions (or the system flows to unexplored fixed points), and the symmetry can be a stopper of such unconventional flows.

column5: Sanghyuk Lee; Ji Li; Chong-Wei Liang; Chun-Yen Shen
column6: On the endpoint estimate for discrete spherical average over sparse sequences
column7: Let $d\ge5$, and let $A_λ$ denote the normalized discrete spherical average on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with squared radius $λ$. For a strictly increasing sequence $(μ_k)$ of positive integers, set $λ_k=μ_k!$ and consider the lacunary maximal operator $A_\star f:=\sup_k|A_{λ_k}f|$. For each fixed $γ>0$, we prove that the estimate \[ \#\{x:A_\star f(x)>α\} \le K\sum_x\frac{|f(x)|}α \left(1+\log^+\frac{|f(x)|}α\right)^γ\] holds with some finite $K$ for all $α>0$ and finitely supported $f$ if and only if \[ \sup_{N\ge2}\frac{\#\{k:μ_k\le N\}}{(1+\log N)^γ}<\infty. \] The summand is interpreted as zero when $f(x)=0$. The case $γ=1$ answers the $\ell\log\ell$ endpoint question of Kesler, Lacey and Mena in the formulation stated above. For $μ_k=2^{2^k}$, these estimates hold for every fixed $γ>0$, but $A_\star$ is not of weak type $(1,1)$. For factorial blocks formed from arbitrary subsets of dyadic grids at widely separated scales, we characterize restricted weak type $(p,p)$, $1<p\le d/(d-1)$, by a uniform covering condition. In particular, for each $1<p_*\le d/(d-1)$, we construct a set of squared radii whose maximal operator is of restricted weak type $(p_*,p_*)$, of strong type $(p,p)$ for $p>p_*$, and unbounded on $\ell^p$ for $1\le p<p_*$.

column6: Delayed Dissipation for Two-Dimensional Vortex Sheets
column7: We quantify viscous energy loss for two-dimensional Delort vortex sheets. Let $u^ν$ be Leray-Hopf solutions on $\mathbb{T}^2$ with uniformly bounded kinetic energy and total vorticity variation, and write $ω_0^ν=μ_0^ν+f_0^ν$, where $μ_0^ν\geq0$ and $f_0^ν$ is bounded in $L^p$, $p>1$. For every fixed $0<δ<T$, $ν\int_δ^T\|ω^ν(t)\|_2^2\,\mathrm{d}t\lesssim_{δ,T}\frac{1}{|\logν|}$. This improves the $O(|\logν|^{-1/2})$ bound of De Rosa and Marcotullio under the same assumptions and thereby disproves their Conjecture 1.6 (arXiv:2602.15670, v1). The proof uses a sharp $L^2$-$H^1$-$H^{-1}$ interpolation inequality for nonnegative densities, retaining the total interaction energy of the positive vorticity rather than only its largest local mass. The bound also remains effective when the observation time grows with the Reynolds number. If the initial velocities are relatively compact in $L^2$, the loss still vanishes whenever $\log T_ν=o(|\logν|)$; in particular, any prescribed energy loss must wait at least until $ν^{-a}$ for some $a>0$. Previous estimates covered only $T_ν=o(\exp(|\logν|^κ))$, $κ<1/2$, so this gives a polynomial lower bound on the energetic lifetime of the inviscid vortex-sheet model.
